reference: Installed file(1) from the isolated reference PATH, compared byte-for-byte with the candidate; deterministic signatures are written by Bash printf. The metadata contract checks Bash type/help builtins against the loadable's documented short description. Custom classifier descriptions and implementation identity are independent contracts, not libmagic parity.
coverage: Bash builtin registration and help metadata
Empty, ASCII text, and opaque-data fallback classes
stdin classification, brief output, path labels, --, and directories
Missing-path status and diagnostic stream behavior
Explicit -E, brief combinations, continuation, no-operand usage and ordinary ENOTDIR errors
exclusions: The classifier's full curated signature catalog is not exhaustively enumerated; the suite samples broad fallback, document, and binary paths.
No fixture uses a host path, real device, network, credentials, or privileged operation; no operation case needs deferral.
The installed reference rejects --error; only -E is supported as the filesystem error option. Full libmagic and detailed ELF output remain outside the custom classifier contract.
Bash type/help and command help/version cases are metadata only and do not count as operation coverage.

cases.purpose: Check through Bash builtins that file is registered as a builtin and that help exposes its documented short description.
cases.script:
type -t file
h=$(help -d file)
case $h in *"Identify file types via magic-byte signatures."*) printf 'help-ok\n' ;; *) exit 1 ;; esac

cases.purpose: Compare brief classification of empty, ordinary ASCII, and short opaque-byte files, covering the basic fallback categories.
cases.script:
: > empty
printf 'plain words\n' > text
printf '\001\002\003' > opaque
file -b empty text opaque

cases.purpose: Check object and array JSON-looking prefixes after optional leading whitespace.
cases.script:
printf '{"key":1}\n' > object
printf '  [1,2]\n' > array
file -b object array

cases.purpose: Compare stable PEM certificate, RSA private-key marker, certificate-request, and PGP message armor labels; the fixtures contain only public marker lines, not key material.
cases.script:
labels=('CERTIFICATE' 'RSA PRIVATE KEY' 'CERTIFICATE REQUEST' 'PGP MESSAGE')
files=(cert rsa-marker request-marker pgp-marker)
for i in "${!labels[@]}"; do
  printf -- '-----BEGIN %s-----\n' "${labels[i]}" > "${files[i]}"
done
file -b cert rsa-marker request-marker pgp-marker

cases.purpose: Check recognition of the conventional 0x55aa DOS/MBR signature at byte offsets 510-511 in a 512-byte relative fixture.
cases.script:
printf '\0%.0s' {1..510} > mbr
printf '\125\252' >> mbr
file -b mbr

cases.purpose: Check that a single stdin operand reads the stream and that brief mode suppresses the input label.
Check aligned labels for a spaced path, option-looking path after --, empty file and directory.
cases.script:
printf 'sample\n' > 'two words'
printf 'dash name\n' > ./-leading
: > empty
mkdir folder
file -- 'two words' ./-leading empty folder

cases.purpose: Continue after a missing operand with a stdout diagnostic and success status by default.
A missing operand uses the reference default diagnostic and success status.
Brief output suppresses labels for both missing and readable operands.
The explicit -E error option reports an error status for a missing operand.
With -E, inspect continuation and diagnostic streams when a missing operand precedes a valid operand.
Alignment uses the literal stdin operand length even though its displayed label is /dev/stdin.
cases.script:
printf 'text\n' > a
printf 'stdin text\n' | file a -

cases.purpose: Label width is recalculated on every builtin invocation.
cases.script:
: > longest_name
: > a
file a longest_name
file a

cases.purpose: A missing intermediate path component follows the same default policy.
The documented small classifier keeps its concise shebang, HTML and Netpbm descriptions for ordinary valid files. These intentional descriptions are not full libmagic output.
cases.script:
printf '#!/bin/sh
printf hello
' > sample.sh
printf '<!doctype html><html><body>hello</body></html>
' > page.html
printf 'P2
1 1
255
0
' > image.pgm
file -b sample.sh page.html image.pgm
cases.stdout:
POSIX shell script
HTML document
Netpbm image data

cases.purpose: Preserve the existing implementation identity banner as a custom metadata contract; do not compare it to the reference version banner or count it as operation coverage.
Long brief mode combines with -E without restoring a path label; processing continues after the missing input.
The explicitly supported -bE short-option bundle gives the same missing-input status and brief diagnostic as separate options.
An invocation without operands returns the installed reference usage status and a diagnostic.
Ordinary ENOTDIR operands follow the same default stdout diagnostic and success status as absent paths.
The installed file reference has no --error alias for -E; reject it with usage status and a diagnostic.
